raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With the DeepSeek-V3.2 encoder (`chat_encoding_spec == "dsv32"`), a thinking-mode request fails with HTTP 400 when it has a `developer` message before its last user turn:

```
DS32EncodingError: Index 2 out of range for messages list of length 2
```

In thinking mode, `encode_messages` first calls `drop_thinking_messages`, which rebuilds the message list without earlier `reasoning_content`. It keeps `user`, `system` and `tool` messages and strips `assistant` ones, but a `developer` message before the last user turn matches neither branch and is dropped. `encode_messages` then loops over the original number of messages, and `render_message` indexes past the end of the shorter list.

The rest of the encoder already treats `developer` as a user turn (`find_last_user_index`, `render_message`), and `serving_chat` passes `developer` messages to this encoder unchanged. Two inputs that hit it:

- an OpenAI-style request with a `developer` instruction followed by a `user` message;
- DeepSeek's multi-turn search-agent format, where each turn is a `developer` message and an assistant reply sits between them.

Chat mode doesn't drop messages and was not affected. DeepSeek's reference `encoding/encoding_dsv32.py` on Hugging Face has the same `["user", "system", "tool"]` list, so the copy here inherited it.

## Modifications

- `drop_thinking_messages` keeps `developer` messages, like `user` messages.
- New `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_encoding_dsv32.py` (CPU suite `base-a-test-cpu`). The encoder had no unit tests, and this case needs no serving fixtures.
  - The test encodes both conversations above in thinking mode and checks that every developer message is rendered and the prompt ends with `<｜Assistant｜><think>`.
  - It fails on `main` with `DS32EncodingError` and passes with the change.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no kernel or model forward change. Requests that worked before render exactly as before, because the change only affects inputs that used to raise.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`pre-commit run` on the changed files passes, including the registered-test checks.)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing docs change.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -300,7 +300,7 @@ def drop_thinking_messages(
     )
     for idx, msg in enumerate(messages):
         role = msg.get("role")
-        if role in ["user", "system", "tool"] or idx >= last_user_idx:
+        if role in ["user", "developer", "system", "tool"] or idx >= last_user_idx:
             messages_wo_thinking.append(msg)
             continue

@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai import encoding_dsv32
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=1, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestEncodingDsv32(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_thinking_mode_keeps_developer_messages(self):
+        """Dropping earlier reasoning in thinking mode must keep developer turns.
+
+        A developer message before the last user-like turn was left out of the
+        thinking-mode message list, so encoding indexed past its end and failed
+        with DS32EncodingError (HTTP 400) instead of rendering the developer turn.
+        """
+        conversations = [
+            # An OpenAI-style developer instruction ahead of the user turn.
+            [
+                {"role": "system", "content": ""},
+                {"role": "developer", "content": "Answer in French."},
+                {"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of Italy?"},
+            ],
+            # A second developer turn after an assistant reply.
+            [
+                {"role": "developer", "content": "Find the population of Rome."},
+                {
+                    "role": "assistant",
+                    "content": "About 2.8M.",
+                    "reasoning_content": "r",
+                },
+                {"role": "developer", "content": "And Milan?"},
+            ],
+        ]
+        for messages in conversations:
+            with self.subTest(roles=[m["role"] for m in messages]):
+                prompt = encoding_dsv32.encode_messages(
+                    messages, thinking_mode="thinking"
+                )
+                for message in messages:
+                    if message["role"] == "developer":
+                        self.assertIn(message["content"], prompt)
+                self.assertTrue(prompt.endswith("<｜Assistant｜><think>"))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
